I am used to keeping the lake healthy by staying within the nine‑per‑boat limit. We have been doing that for three years. The lake hasn't shown any sign of decline; the stock seems fine. So there's no reason to restrict myself any further than the usual nine. I also know Yuki has been off fishing for a couple of rounds and has zero catch, but that doesn't affect the lake; it just means there will be fewer boats on the water tomorrow. I need income. I was idle this round and didn't take any fish. If I stay at the dock again, I will lose another day of potential catch. The lake is healthy, so there's room for another round of nine tons. The group will be four people tomorrow; we can each aim for nine tons. That would remove 36 tons, bringing the lake to about 118.1 tons, still healthy.

I noticed that the lake is down to 7.4 tons, and the condition is described as near collapse. I have no catch this round, so if I stay at the dock I’ll lose another day of income and the fish will probably stay scarce. James has agreed to take only two tons, but that still leaves a lot of fish to be caught by the others. I need to decide whether to risk the lake or to stay and wait. I think I can still catch a small amount without pushing the stock to zero, and the loss of another day without income is more immediate than the risk of overfishing a few more tons. I will go out tomorrow. I will aim to keep my take low—perhaps one ton or less—and I’ll check in with James to see if he can cut even further. That way I get something, and we all reduce pressure on the lake.
